title: Purity for a finite normal cover over a local base of dimension at most one
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal local domain, with closed point $a\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ (normal means integral domain and integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]; local means it has a unique maximal ideal). Let $q:L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be quasi-compact, quasi-separated, smooth with geometrically connected fibres [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $V\subset\operatorname{Spec}A$ be the open whose points are exactly those different from $a$. Let $n:N\to L$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with every local ring of $N$ a normal domain. Assume the open $n^{-1}(q^{-1}(V))$ is dense in $N$ and $n|_{q^{-1}(V)}$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $W\subset L$ be open and $x\in W$ satisfy $q(x)=a$ and $n|_W$ etale. If $\dim A\le1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], then $n$ is etale.

proof.text: If A has dimension zero it is a field and V is empty. Density forces N empty, hence n is etale. In the other case a normal Noetherian local domain of dimension one is a DVR. Smoothness makes its closed fibre a regular effective Cartier divisor; smoothness with geometric connectedness makes that fibre integral.

The open W meets the closed fibre and hence contains its generic point. The punctured finite etale cover is unramified at that point, and away from the divisor it is already etale. Tag 0EYE therefore supplies a finite etale cover E of L extending the punctured cover.

L and E are normal. Density excludes a component of N supported on the closed fibre; every generic component of N lies over a generic component of L, since n is etale over the puncture. On each affine component, both E and N are the integral closure of the base algebra in the same generic algebra: their rings are integral over the base, and any element integral over the base is integral over each normal finite algebra and therefore belongs to it. The resulting isomorphisms agree on overlaps and give N isomorphic to E over L. Consequently n is etale.
